changelog: Paraphrased C3 to shorten and sharpen the contra-risk prompt so it is quicker to apply while preserving scope/negation/contrast guidance.
Paraphrased C5 to compress the cohesion guidance into a concise checklist-style prompt and free space for new rules.
Paraphrased C7 to keep the English-specific cues but shorter and more direct about verbs, subordinators, pronouns, lists, and punctuation.
Inserted a new explicit 'Contra checklist' unit (after C5) implementing the critic's finding that a single disambiguating element on the right should raise contra toward 1.
Inserted a new 'Connectives' unit (after C5) implementing the critic's finding that isolating connectives from their completing clause raises both contra and cohesion penalty.
findings: The scorer underestimates contra-risk when the right-hand fragment contains the single disambiguating, negating, or specifying element (negation, quantifier/ordinal, list continuation, or the complement that decides truth) that determines the truth-conditions of the already-heard left fragment.

The scorer treats coordinating/connective words (but, and, while, however, respectively, etc.) too lightly and therefore misses that cuts adjacent to these connectors typically indicate tight dependency or contrast and often carry high contra/cohesion risk.

diagnosis.why: The new items pushed the model to cut earlier so that finite verbs, short disambiguating words, and connective words often landed alone on the right fragment — e.g. subjects separated from verbs and list items or contrast markers isolated — which reduces cohesion and therefore lowered H_set, with the harm concentrated on very short pieces (≤3–≤7-word bins).
diagnosis.lesson: A later revision should avoid wording that rewards isolating single-word disambiguators, connectives, or finite verbs into very-short right fragments (especially in ≤3–≤7 bins) because that produces many harmful subject/verb and list splits.
